newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico asks Zapatista rebels to return to talks.
newsitem.headline: Mexico asks Zapatista rebels to return to talks.

text.p: Mexico asked Zapatista rebels on Monday to restart peace talks that broke down last week after guerrillas accused the government of not negotiating seriously.

"(Zapatistas) have said they do not believe violence is the answer. To honour that commitment, we hope the (Zapatista National Liberation Army) will reconsider its position and return to talks," the Interior Ministry said in a statement.
"The negotiating process is not negotiable ... In Chiapas, the government maintains its promise to find a peaceful settlement to the conflict," the statement said.

Zapatista forces pulled out of the talks a week ago, accusing the government of intentionally stalling the peace process to allow its army to step up military pressure on the rebels in southern Chiapas state.

The government said it has done everything it can to placate the rebels during peace talks, which have dragged on in fits and starts since the Zapatistas launched a brief rebellion in early 1994 that killed at least 145 people.

Officials so far have been at pains to differentiate the Zapatistas, who have now renounced violence, from a new rebel group, the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR), which sprang up at the end of June fighting for a Marxist state and has so far refused to negotiate.

The government has freed several alleged Zapatista leaders from jail, allowed the rebels to hold a national poll on their eventual transition to a political force and carried out an earlier agreement on Indian rights, the ministry said.
"The EZLN said the federal government has done everything it can to prevent progress in peace: they lie," the ministry's statement said.
Officials have accused the rebels of suspending talks to step up pressure on the government following the surprise appearance of the EPR.
